resources.string: Hotspot devices only · Phone apps bypass WireGuard
TunnelSpot sends Wi-Fi hotspot clients through your selected WireGuard profile. The phone itself keeps its normal internet connection. No root and no software or proxy settings on clients.

Experimental · Android 13+

Set your Wi-Fi hotspot name and password in Android settings, then leave the hotspot off. Import a WireGuard profile with an IPv4 address, IPv4 DNS server, and AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0. Toggle it on to start both WireGuard and the hotspot.

The built-in helper runs as Android ADB shell, not root. After helper startup you can disable Wireless debugging; hotspot control uses Binder, not a persistent ADB connection. Restart the helper after reboot, app restart, or app update. Pair again if Android forgets this app. No companion app is needed.

This version shares IPv4 (TCP, UDP and DNS). Native IPv6 is not advertised. Providers must supply a standard WireGuard config; OpenVPN and proprietary VPN apps are not supported.

Hidden tethering APIs vary by device. TunnelSpot checks the selected upstream and attempts to stop Wi-Fi sharing if it changes. This is NOT a guaranteed system kill switch: Android may briefly fall back to another upstream, especially if a process crashes. Do not rely on it for leak-sensitive use until verified on your device.
Built-in helper connected. You can turn Wireless debugging off. Import a profile, then turn its switch on.

Start the built-in helper below. No root or companion app is required. An unused helper stops after ten minutes.

1. Enable Developer options (tap Build number seven times in Android settings), then enable Wireless debugging while connected to Wi-Fi.
2. Tap Start pairing notification below. In Wireless debugging, open Pair device with pairing code. Keep that dialog open; pull down notifications and enter its six-digit code in the TunnelSpot notification.
3. Return here and tap Start built-in helper. Discovery finds the local connection port; enter the port from the main Wireless debugging screen if discovery fails. This is NOT the pairing port.
4. After the helper connects, turn Wireless debugging off. The helper stays available until stopped or the app/phone restarts.

Pairing authorizes this app with ADB shell privileges, broader than a normal app. TunnelSpot connects only to this phone (127.0.0.1); it provides no remote shell or arbitrary command entry. Its ADB identity is encrypted using Android Keystore and excluded from backup. To revoke access, forget TunnelSpot under Wireless debugging → Paired devices.
Manual alternative (split screen): keep Android’s pairing dialog open beside TunnelSpot and enter its port and code below. Pairing ports and codes expire when the dialog closes.
Discovering local ADB and starting the helper…
Allow notifications for pairing, or use the split-screen manual alternative.
Open Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. Keep the dialog open; return to this notification to enter the code.
Local pairing service found. Tap Enter code and submit the six-digit code while Android’s pairing dialog stays open.
Pairing dialog is no longer available. Open a new pairing dialog and try again.
Pairing with Android’s local ADB service…
Pairing failed. Open a new pairing dialog and try again. If discovery is unavailable, use manual split-screen pairing.
Paired. Return to TunnelSpot and tap Start built-in helper.
